subject: Interim notice: elevated inference tail latency affecting Aurora Biotech API calls
messages:
From: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
To: sam.patel@aurorabiotech.com, support@aurorabiotech.com
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-15T08:02:00-08:00
Subject: Interim notice: elevated inference tail latency affecting Aurora Biotech API calls

Hi Sam / Aurora team,

We’re reaching out to let you know we’ve observed an elevated tail-latency event impacting a subset of hosted inference requests from 07:45–08:00 PST this morning. Affected calls experienced intermittent multi-second tails (95th-99th percentile) on generation endpoints used by your integration. Early analysis shows the majority of affected requests were to the /v1/generate route with longer context windows (~4k tokens).

Immediate actions we’ve taken:
- Diverted new short-sequence traffic to a warmed model pool to reduce queuing.
- Enabled conservative batching limits for your tenant to lower head-of-line blocking.
- Flagged the cluster for priority investigation; engineering is onboarded on the bridge.

We don’t yet have a full root cause, but we suspect transient queue backpressure in the host batch scheduler when larger KV caches are primed concurrently. I’ll follow up with a customer-facing summary to post on status.redwood once we confirm the scope.

For planning: can you confirm whether any mission-critical ML routes (besides /v1/generate) were impacted for you and whether you’ve observed client-side retries or timeouts? If you’d prefer, we can open a ticket for account-level throttling so you can move traffic to a dedicated fallback.

Attachments: minimal incident metrics snapshot (hosted-queue-metrics-20261115.log)

—
Grace O’Connor
Head of Customer Solutions, Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0147

From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@aurorabiotech.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: support@aurorabiotech.com
Date: 2026-11-15T08:21:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Interim notice: elevated inference tail latency affecting Aurora Biotech API calls

Hi Grace — thanks for the heads up.

We did see increased 5xx and client-side retry spikes starting ~07:48. The majority were from our batch ingestion pipeline calling /v1/generate with ~3.5k token contexts. We temporarily scaled down ingestion and saw errors reduce. No production customer-facing outages reported yet, but internal automation did trigger backfills.

If you think dedicated fallback routing helps, we’re open to that. Also please keep us posted on any ETA for a permanent remediation — our CS and SRE teams are standing by.

—
Sam Patel
Platform Lead, Aurora Biotech
sam.patel@aurorabiotech.com
From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-15T09:05:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Interim notice: elevated inference tail latency affecting Aurora Biotech API calls

Grace / team — quick tech notes from the bridge:

Observations:
- Spike in queue length and CPU saturation on a subset of GPU hosts serving mixed long-context requests (peak 07:46–07:59 PST).
- KV cache priming combined with large batch windows caused amplified memory pressure; we saw OOM-adjacent behavior leading to longer scheduler retries.
- No permanent instance crashes; autoscaler kept hosts but responses were slower due to repeated internal scheduling attempts.

Actions performed (live):
- Reduced max_batch_tokens for tenant routing to 50% for the next 60 minutes.
- Reduced concurrency cap on affected pools and warmed a standby pool with lower batching sensitivity.
- Flushed a subset of long-lived KV cache entries to prevent re-priming spikes.

Short-term mitigation seems to have brought p95 down to acceptable bounds for most routes. I’ve attached our logs/metrics snapshot (hosted-queue-metrics-20261115.log) and a quick CSV timeline (incident-timeline-aurorabiotech-20261115.csv).

Next steps we’re proposing:
1) Backfill a scheduling patch to better isolate long-context priming from short context traffic. (Engineering P0, owner: infra-scheduler team)
2) Provide Aurora an optional routing flag to pin critical routes to a low-latency warmed pool. (Product + Solutions)
3) Draft a post-incident note for status.redwood with customer-facing impact and ETA for permanent fix.

I’ll loop in infra-scheduler for an ETA; preliminary estimate is a code fix + canary within 48–72 hours.

—
Markus Klein
Director, Runtime Engineering
From: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
To: sam.patel@aurorabiotech.com, support@aurorabiotech.com
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-15T10:02:00-08:00
Subject: Customer-facing status update (for Aurora Biotech) — brief summary and next steps

Sam — thanks for the quick response and for scaling down ingestion while we stabilized. Below is a concise summary you can use internally; we also posted a short advisory on status.redwood (link below).

Status (interim):
- Impact window: 2026-11-15T07:45–~08:05 PST.
- Symptom: intermittent elevated tail latency (95th–99th) and a small increase in client retries for /v1/generate with long contexts.
- Scope: subset of hosted inference customers using long-context generation; Aurora Biotech observed client-side retries but no sustained production outage.

What we did:
- Immediate routing adjustments (conservative batching + warmed pool) to reduce queuing.
- Short-term limits applied to tenant-specific batching and concurrency.
- Engineering triage started; suspected batch scheduler + KV priming interaction.

What we’ll deliver:
- Patch to scheduler to better quarantine large-context priming (ETA 48–72 hours).
- Optional routing flag for critical routes to pin to low-latency warmed pools (ETA in the week).
- Post-incident summary and remediation plan; we’ll share a draft for your review.

Compensation: we will evaluate token-credit compensation for any measurable customer impact and will follow up with a formal credit proposal via your account rep.

Status link: https://status.redwood.inference/incidents/2026-11-15-aurora-degrade

If you want a short blurb for your internal status page, you can use: "Redwood observed a brief period of elevated inference tail latency affecting long-context generation routes. Traffic was routed to warmed pools and the issue has been stabilized; a code fix is in progress."

—
Grace O’Connor
Head of Customer Solutions

From: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
To: sam.patel@aurorabiotech.com, support@aurorabiotech.com
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-16T16:45:00-08:00
Subject: Post-incident summary & next steps — Aurora Biotech event (2026-11-15)

Sam / Aurora team — thank you for your patience. Engineering completed the initial fix and we published a postmortem draft for internal review. Below is the customer-facing summary and the actions we’ll take next week.

Summary (final):
- Impact: Brief period of elevated tail latency for long-context generation requests between 07:45–08:05 PST on 2026-11-15. The issue increased client-side retries for Aurora’s ingestion pipeline but did not cause persistent production outages.
- Root cause (engineer-validated): Scheduler interaction with KV cache priming under bursty long-context traffic created transient memory pressure and scheduler retries, increasing response tails.

Remediation completed/ongoing:
- Deployed a low-latency routing flag (customer pinning) for critical routes — completed as an opt-in toggle for Aurora.
- Scheduler patch merged; canary rollout scheduled to a subset of clusters tomorrow (2026-11-17).
- Added telemetry to proactively detect re-priming spikes and auto-throttle large-context batches.

Customer impact & compensation:
- We’ll provide a token credit equating to the estimated excess retries for the impacted window. Your account rep (Ben Carter) will follow up with the credit calculation and formal A/R entry.

Attachments: postmortem-draft-aurorabiotech-20261116.md (draft), incident-timeline-aurorabiotech-20261115.csv
Links: https://docs.redwood.inference/s/INC-2026-113-aurora-postmortem-draft

If you’d like to schedule a 30-minute debrief with engineering and product next week to walk through the postmortem and the routing toggle, suggest times and we’ll put something on the calendar.

Apologies again for the disruption — we’ll keep you updated as the canary progresses.

—
Grace O’Connor
Head of Customer Solutions, Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0147
